content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: 12 verified, 0 errors.

**Diagnosis** (saved in `diagnosis.json`: invariant / bridge): the loop invariant at line 51 in `mfirstMaximum` was `forall k :: 0<=k<i ==> v[i] > v[k] - 1`. For integers that is the same as `v[i] >= v[k]`. When the loop ends, Dafny knows only the invariant and the negated loop condition, so this non-strict fact can't prove the strict postcondition `forall l :: 0<=l<i ==> v[i] > v[l]`, which says `i` is the *first* maximum. The counterexample shows this: the value 5853 appears at several indices, and a non-strict invariant can't rule out returning a later one.

**Fix:** I made the invariant strict: `forall k :: 0<=k<i ==> v[i] > v[k]`. It holds at the start because `i = 0` makes the range empty. It stays true because `i` only moves to `j` when `v[j]` is strictly greater than every earlier element. At exit it gives the postcondition directly. Nothing else in the file was changed.
